pages.title: Superacids
pages.text: $(thing)Superacids$()$(br2)Acids a million million times stronger than sulfuric - strong enough to protonate almost anything.

$(thing)Insight$(): 50$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Electrochemistry, High-Energy Particle Physics.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 2 Electride Crystal.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): A weakly basic indicator B is dissolved in a superacid and partly protonated to BH⁺. The acidity is measured by how far the protonation goes. Write the acidity function from the standard free energy of deprotonation of BH⁺ (converted to a base-10 logarithm) plus the log of the ratio of unprotonated to protonated indicator.
